Nonparametric regression via DNN rank weights

Source: R/user-dnn-npr.R
np_dnn.Rd

Estimate a localized nonparametric mean by combining observed outcomes with DNN-based local weights.

Usage

np_dnn(
  data = NULL,
  x_cols = NULL,
  y_col = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  X = NULL,
  Y = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  distance = "l2",
  method = c("exact", "asymp"),
  k = 1L,
  s = NULL,
  tuning = NULL,
  tuning_mode = c("default", "grid"),
  normalize = TRUE,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = c("fast", "loo", "none"),
  ctx = NULL,
  return = c("W")
)

Arguments

data

Optional data frame containing covariates and outcome columns. Column names must be non-missing, non-empty, and unique.

x_cols

Names or indices of covariate columns in data.

y_col

Name or index of the outcome column in data.

y

Optional numeric outcome vector of length n. In the data-frame interface, use this instead of y_col.

X

Numeric matrix (n x p) for the matrix interface.

Y

Numeric outcome vector of length n for the matrix interface.

X0

Numeric matrix (m x p) of target points; mutually exclusive with x0.

x0

Numeric vector of length p for a single target point.

distance

Distance name or specification (for example "l2").

method

One of "exact" or "asymp" for DNN weights.

k

Integer DNN neighbour count inside each size-s subsample. The paper theory uses k = 1 (the default).

s

Integer kernel order (undersmoothing parameter), or NULL. When both s and tuning are NULL (the default), s is resolved from the paper undersmoothing rule tuning_dnn_paper(), \(s = \lfloor 0.4 n^{(k_x+1)/(k_x+2)} \rfloor\). Note that small fixed values such as s = 1 (or k = s) yield uniform weights and hence no localization; a warning is emitted in that case.

tuning

Optional kernel-order tuning specification. When supplied, s must be omitted and is resolved from tuning.

tuning_mode

One of "default" or "grid". "default" evaluates the default s only. "grid" evaluates the feasible candidates from tuning, or from tuning_dnn_paper() when tuning is omitted, and stores candidate-level estimates, standard errors, diagnostics, and metadata in tuning_grid. Grid mode cannot be combined with explicit s.

normalize

Logical; renormalize columns of W to sum to 1.

se

Logical; compute delete-1 jackknife standard errors.

jackknife

One of "fast", "loo", or "none". "fast" (default) uses cached full-sample ranks with delete-1 rank updates, "loo" recomputes leave-one-out weights directly, and "none" skips SEs.

ctx

Optional context passed to distance and ranking components.

return

Optional extras in addition to the always-returned mu, se, and meta. Allowed values: c("W", "ranks", "ord", "dx", "y", "ess", "neighbors", "tuning"). The neighbors extra returns the first k nearest observations used inside each size-s subsample, not the full DNN weight support.

Value

An object of class np_result with components:

  • mu: estimated local mean values at target points;

  • se: optional jackknife standard errors;

  • x0: the m x p matrix of evaluation points, with covariate column names propagated from the training data when available;

  • meta: metadata (n, m, p, k, s, method, distance);

  • tuning_grid: in grid mode, a list with candidates, estimates, diagnostics, and meta tables. Candidate diagnostics report top-5 weight concentration separately from the estimator's k;

  • optional extras requested via return.

Details

Two interfaces are supported.

  1. Data-frame interface (recommended): pass data, x_cols, and either y_col or y (exactly one).

  2. Matrix interface: pass X, one of X0 or x0, and Y.

For method = "exact", DNN weights are computed from the full rank permutation at each target. The exact support extends through rank n - s + k (n - s + 1 in the paper-faithful k = 1 case); this is not an s-nearest-neighbor truncation. The "fast" jackknife option reuses the full-sample rank matrix and updates ranks under deletion.

tuning_mode = "default" evaluates only the default kernel order and preserves the ordinary scalar-fit return shape. tuning_mode = "grid" evaluates the feasible candidates in tuning, or the paper default tuning grid when tuning is omitted, and attaches a tidy tuning_grid payload. The primary mu, se, meta, and optional extras such as W, ranks, ess, and neighbors remain anchored to the default candidate. Full per-candidate weight matrices are not stored. Candidate diagnostics include ess, max_weight, top_n, top5_weight_share, and degenerate; top_n is fixed at 5 and is independent of the estimator's k.

See also

weights_dnn(), np_demo_data().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 60
x_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2)
y_vec <- x_mat[, 1] - 0.5 * x_mat[, 2] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
out <- np_dnn(
  X = x_mat, x0 = c(0, 0), Y = y_vec,
  distance = "l2", method = "exact", k = 1L, s = 3L,
  se = FALSE, return = c("W", "ess")
)
out$mu
#> [1] 0.05695052
